thread.title: Apple: What It Will Take to Reach $1 Trillion

author: Andrew Bary
title: Apple: What It Will Take to Reach $1 Trillion
text:
By Andrew Bary Aug. 1, 2018 11:59 a.m. ET Apple (AAPL) is nearing an historic $1 trillion market value following its strong earnings report Tuesday for the June quarter. But its quest to hit that mark is being slowed by its massive stock-buyback program, which is steadily reducing its outstanding shares.
Apple CEO Tim Cook Apple shares are up $10.07 to $200.36, a 5.3% gain, in trading Wednesday, putting its market value at $970 billion. It had earlier hit a record $201.32. Apple needs to hit a share price of $206.49 to reach the $1 trillion milestone, according to Howard Silverblatt , the senior index analyst at S&P Dow Jones Indices.
This price is based on the share count of 4.843 billion on Apple’s balance sheet for June, released Tuesday as part of the earnings release. That share count, however, is likely to fall slightly when Apple releases its quarterly 10-Q report, because of the company’s ongoing share-buyback program.
It likely will show a share count as of late July. The 10-Q is expected to be issued later today, based on the company’s recent pattern of releasing the 10-Q a day after the earnings release.
Given the pace of Apple buybacks, the share count listed in the 10-Q could be close to 4.825 billion, pushing up the needed share price for Apple to hit $1 trillion to about $207 a share. Apple bought back $20.8 billion of stock in the June quarter, its second-largest quarterly buyback ever, trailing only the $22.8 billion repurchased in the March quarter.
Silverblatt notes that while a company’s market value is based on the share count on the balance sheet, the most widely followed earnings calculation uses the average diluted shares outstanding, which for Apple was 4.927 billion in the latest quarter. The diluted share count includes employee stock awards and other factors such as convertible debt that lifts the share count.
